nodes.label: Ruffle Runtime Integrity Verification
nodes.rationale: The archive and every extracted runtime and license file are validated before packaging.

nodes.label: Tokenized Loopback Adapter Security
nodes.rationale: Exact file and origin allowlists, random tokens, bounded tunnels, destination checks, and privacy-safe logging constrain the browser-to-game adapter.

nodes.label: Ruffle and WebView2 Upstream Host Boundary
nodes.norm_label: ruffle and webview2 upstream host boundary
nodes.rationale: Stock Ruffle desktop lacks Grimoire's callback ABI, while the web runtime and WebView2 jointly provide JavaScript ExternalInterface and a synchronous host-object boundary.

nodes.label: Flash.ocx Compatibility Fallback
nodes.rationale: Flash.ocx remains the recommended default and is used when the verified Ruffle payload or WebView2 Runtime is unavailable or emulator compatibility differs.

nodes.label: Graph-First Repository Navigation
nodes.rationale: Graph reflection and scoped queries should identify relevant areas before broad search or source reads.

nodes.label: Mobile Architecture Boundary
nodes.rationale: Android modules depend inward through neutral model and domain layers and must not depend on WinForms, ActiveX, desktop updater state, or mutable desktop output.

nodes.label: Privacy and Local-Machine Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Account data, bot libraries, logs, packet bodies, credentials, and machine-specific paths are private and must not be scanned, committed, or reported without explicit scope.

nodes.label: Bounded Data-Only GBot Parsing
nodes.rationale: Parsing must not load runtime types or use reflection, and unknown commands may be inspected but never executed.

nodes.label: Android GBot Inspection-Only Milestone
nodes.rationale: Android initially supports safe inspection rather than execution or rewriting until semantic round-trip coverage exists.

nodes.label: Per-Session Game State and Packet Dispatch
nodes.norm_label: per-session game state and packet dispatch

nodes.label: Desktop Multi-Client Research and Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: desktop multi-client research and implementation plan

nodes.label: ClientSessionContext Compatibility Facade
nodes.rationale: AsyncLocal-scoped session routing preserves legacy static APIs during migration while preventing background work from following later UI selection.

nodes.label: Toolbar Isolation Contract
nodes.rationale: Changing the selected client may change displayed controls but must never retarget an existing bot, packet handler, timer, login flow, or asynchronous action.

nodes.label: Data-Only Permission Boundary
nodes.rationale: Describing interchange data does not grant permission to connect to, modify, automate, or redistribute an Artix client.

nodes.label: Sensitive Data Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Contracts must not contain credentials, account labels, private bot files, packet bodies, or machine paths.

nodes.label: Language-Neutral Compatibility Boundary
nodes.rationale: Neutral contracts and fixtures let desktop and Android validate identical behavior without importing each other's runtime or UI framework.

nodes.label: Bot-Safe Inactive-Client Throttling
nodes.rationale: Inactive-client FPS may be reduced only when its bot is not running and must be restored before the client becomes active.

nodes.label: Measured FPS Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Actual FPS must be sampled from ENTER_FRAME rather than inferred from Stage.frameRate, which is only a target.

nodes.label: Rendering and Performance Profile
nodes.rationale: A CPU/GPU/Both selector would misrepresent what Grimoire controls, so presentation mode, quality, FPS, and inactive-client behavior are exposed separately.

nodes.label: Release Supply-Chain Hardening
nodes.rationale: Smoke-test gating, version tags, signatures, checksums, provenance, and clean-machine tests reduce release risk.

nodes.label: Pre-Tag Continuous Integration
nodes.rationale: PR and main checks catch compatibility regressions before a release tag publishes packages.

nodes.label: v1.5 Compatibility Preservation
nodes.rationale: Legacy GBot loading, user data, per-client isolation, and internal assembly identity remain unchanged while access and diagnostics improve.

nodes.label: v1.3 Compatibility Preservation
nodes.rationale: Legacy GBot serialization, internal assembly identity, user files, and app-local Flash behavior are preserved while new settings and UI features are added.

nodes.label: Allowlisted Runtime File Verification
nodes.rationale: The build verifies both the package archive and every allowlisted runtime file before copying artifacts into application output.

nodes.label: Optional Ruffle with Flash Fallback
nodes.rationale: Ruffle is optional, while Flash.ocx remains the default compatibility path.

nodes.label: User Bot Separation
nodes.rationale: User bots live outside the release payload so application updates do not overwrite them.

nodes.label: Official v1.1.0 Packages
nodes.rationale: The MSI and portable ZIP should be downloaded only from the official repository because repacks are not verified.

nodes.label: Privacy-Safe Bug Reporting
nodes.rationale: Reports must omit passwords, tokens, account-vault contents, and other private data while supplying reproducible steps.

nodes.label: Problem-First Feature Design
nodes.rationale: Requests should explain the user problem before proposing an implementation.

nodes.label: Origin Restriction and Per-Address Rate Limit
nodes.norm_label: origin restriction and per-address rate limit

nodes.label: Website Report Privacy Review
nodes.rationale: Passwords, account-vault data, tokens, usernames, room names, and other private information must be removed before submitting a website-prepared report.

nodes.label: Private Security Advisory Routing
nodes.rationale: Security vulnerabilities belong in a private GitHub Security Advisory rather than a public issue.

nodes.label: Commit-Pinned Pages Actions
nodes.rationale: Third-party actions are referenced by immutable commit hashes while retaining human-readable version comments.

nodes.label: Browser Credential Isolation
nodes.rationale: A Cloudflare Worker keeps the repository-scoped GitHub credential out of the static site and visitor browser.

nodes.label: Authenticated GBot Attachment Handoff
nodes.rationale: Selected GBots remain local and use GitHub's authenticated issue composer because the anonymous issue API does not provide a safe attachment flow.

nodes.label: Anonymous GBot Attachment Rejection
nodes.rationale: GBot files stay local because GitHub's issue API has no safe anonymous attachment flow.

nodes.label: Safe Worker Health Check
nodes.rationale: GET /health validates the live service without creating a public test issue.

nodes.label: Repository-Scoped GitHub Credential
nodes.rationale: The fine-grained token is limited to repository metadata and issue access and is stored only as an encrypted Cloudflare secret.

nodes.label: Per-Client Loopback HTTP and Socket Transport
nodes.norm_label: per-client loopback http and socket transport

nodes.label: Flash Compatibility Baseline
nodes.rationale: Private registration-free Flash.ocx remains the default while Ruffle is opt-in and must fail closed without interrupting existing clients or bots.

nodes.label: Pre-Ready Safe Flash Fallback
nodes.rationale: Only a pre-ready Ruffle client with no active login or bot may be replaced automatically; ready, logged-in, or bot-running clients are marked faulted instead.

nodes.label: Verified Ruffle Supply Chain
nodes.rationale: The official package, individual runtime files, licenses, WebView2 dependencies, staging payload, and updater requirements are pinned and validated.

nodes.label: Selected Ruffle WebView2 Adapter
nodes.rationale: The self-hosted web runtime uses supported public Ruffle APIs and WebView2 while avoiding maintenance of a Rust fork.

nodes.label: Default App-Local Flash Engine
nodes.rationale: Registration-free COM preserves the existing ActiveX bridge without registering or replacing system Flash and remains the recommended compatibility path.

nodes.label: Experimental Direct and GPU Presentation Requests
nodes.norm_label: experimental direct and gpu presentation requests

nodes.label: Rendering Profile Qualification Gate
nodes.rationale: An experimental mode qualifies only without rendering, input, focus, bridge, or isolation regressions and with repeatable CPU or frame-time improvement.

nodes.label: Archive and OCX Hash Pinning
nodes.rationale: Both the downloaded archive and extracted ActiveX control are verified independently before use.

nodes.label: Private Enforcement Reporting
nodes.rationale: Sensitive conduct complaints are reported privately to protect the reporter and preserve confidentiality.

nodes.label: Secret and Runtime Artifact Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Contributions must not contain credentials, account data, private bot data, Flash.ocx, or build output.

nodes.label: Official Release Distribution
nodes.rationale: Only official GitHub releases are maintained and verified; third-party mirrors and repacks may contain malicious modifications.

nodes.label: Official Downloads Only
nodes.rationale: Unofficial mirrors, repacks, and installers are unverified and may contain malware or modified binaries.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Suspected vulnerabilities are disclosed privately so maintainers can investigate and release a fix before public disclosure.

nodes.label: Grimoire Exodus v1.1.0 Code and Performance Audit
nodes.norm_label: grimoire exodus v1.1.0 code and performance audit

nodes.label: Grimoire Exodus v1.2.0 Improvement and Feature Research
nodes.norm_label: grimoire exodus v1.2.0 improvement and feature research

nodes.label: Run-Owned Bot Session Model
nodes.rationale: Immutable run state and awaited shutdown prevent cancelled loops from observing a newer run's token and configuration.

nodes.label: Bounded Batched Logging
nodes.rationale: Unbounded UI text and synchronous marshaling increase memory and append cost throughout long sessions.

nodes.label: Instrument Flash Before Optimizing
nodes.rationale: Compatibility-sensitive caching and batching should follow measurements of the synchronous XML, COM, and JSON boundary.

nodes.label: Pre-Indexed Packet Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Handler indexing belongs at infrequent registration time instead of allocating and scanning for every packet.

nodes.label: Explicit Plugin Trust Controls
nodes.rationale: Automatically loaded DLLs execute with full trust and cannot truly unload from the default AppDomain.

nodes.label: AQW Loading and Compatibility State Machine
nodes.norm_label: aqw loading and compatibility state machine
nodes.rationale: Named loading stages and explicit failure states distinguish progress from incompatibility and allow automation to fail closed.

nodes.label: Bounded Packet and Log Ingress
nodes.rationale: A capped text control is insufficient when its producer queue remains unbounded during packet bursts.

nodes.label: Plugin Trust Model
nodes.rationale: Safe-start, explicit enablement, publisher and hash display, quarantine, and a future process boundary reduce plugin risk.

nodes.label: Privacy-Safe Diagnostic Export
nodes.rationale: Support bundles should redact local paths, bots, account identifiers, rooms, and packet bodies while preserving useful diagnostics.

nodes.label: User Data and Legacy Format Preservation
nodes.norm_label: user data and legacy format preservation
nodes.rationale: User bots, settings, plugins, sets, recovery data, and account-vault data remain outside the installation payload and survive updates.
